description.narrative: The Recipient will enter into a two-year cooperative agreement with the Wildlife Without Borders - Latin America and Caribbea (WWB-LAC) program to develop and implement a new Master in Conservation Practice (MCP) in 2013 by leveraging the highly interdisciplinary, hands-on approach incorporated in the Master in Development Practice (MDP) but with a stronger focus on biodiversity conservation. The MCP will address the real-world training needs of professionals active in conservation in Latin America and the Caribbean by developing and strengthening the students' competencies (knowledge, abilities, and attitudes) to deliver biodiversity conservation at the local level in a participatory, equitable, and sustainable way. their capacities to mainstream biodiversity conservation into sustainable development at the local level. The MCP will be a Professional Master's degree taught by experienced conservation professionals. The core competencies of the program will be: 1) ecological processes and biodiversity conservation; 2) facilitation of participatory processes; 3) designing, planning, implementing, and monitoring and evaluation of organizations, processes and projects; 4) promotion and support of local entrepreneurial inititives; 5) knowledge management and training skills based on intercultural dialogue methods; 6) conflict resolution; 7) promotion of equity; and 8) support and development of local governance as articulated within local and national policy and laws. FWS funds will provide scholarships to cover the tuition of 6 students over a two-year period.
